slow_main_sensor.title: Grid power sensor updates too slowly
slow_main_sensor.description: The configured grid sensor {sensor} updates about every {observed_interval} seconds. Updates every {warning_interval} seconds or more are slower than recommended and may reduce regulation quality. Omnibattery still follows the latest reading until it is more than {stale_limit} seconds old. Use a faster sensor if you need tighter real-time control.

price_data_unusable.title: Price data unusable
price_data_unusable.description: Omnibattery could not parse usable price slots from {sensor} for over {minutes} minutes (status: {status}). Price-aware charging is inactive: dynamic-pricing scheduling and the price-aware charge-delay release fall back to their no-price behaviour. Check that the sensor is available and that its price attribute is a list of entries; a template sensor must emit ISO-8601 timestamps, because a rendered Python datetime cannot be converted back into a list.

solar_forecast_unusable.title: Solar forecast unusable
solar_forecast_unusable.description: The configured solar forecast sensor {sensor} has been unavailable or unreadable for over {minutes} minutes. Omnibattery keeps running, but every feature that depends on the forecast is now blind: the charge delay unlocks for the rest of the day, grid-charge decisions assume no sun at all and may book grid slots you do not need, and remaining-solar estimates read as 0 kWh. Check the sensor or the integration that provides it.

solar_forecast_remaining_recommended.title: Use a remaining solar forecast
solar_forecast_remaining_recommended.description: {sensor} is a legacy whole-day solar forecast. Omnibattery still supports it, but past forecast errors can make intraday decisions inaccurate. Configure the provider's "remaining today" forecast sensor in Omnibattery options for a more accurate remaining-solar calculation.

three_phase_manual_mode.title: Three-phase protection can be bypassed by manual commands
three_phase_manual_mode.description: Three-phase protection is enabled, but manual register or manual time-slot commands can write directly to a battery without the automatic phase envelope. Keep those commands within the configured phase limits.

migrate_legacy.title: Migrate from Marstek Venus
migrate_legacy.description: Found {count} existing Marstek Venus configuration(s). Migrating to Omnibattery keeps all your entities, history and settings intact. Continue?

user.title: Configure Omnibattery
user.description: Select the sensor that measures grid import/export power. Optionally, configure the solar forecast sensor for advanced features.

data_description.consumption_sensor: Real-time sensor for imported (+) or exported (-) grid power. Updates every 1-2 seconds are recommended. Slower sensors are accepted, but delayed readings reduce regulation quality; the latest reading is followed for up to 65 seconds.
data_description.offgrid_power_sensor: Separate W/kW meter for the backed-up circuit. It must differ from the normal grid sensor. Configuring it exposes a software switch that selects this source for control and statistics; it does not enable the battery's physical off-grid/EPS port.
data_description.offgrid_meter_inverted: Enable when the off-grid sensor uses the opposite convention: positive = export and negative = consumption. This setting applies only while off-grid meter mode is active.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Legacy sensor providing the whole-day solar forecast. Existing installations can keep using it during the transition; prefer Remaining Today for new configurations.
data_description.solar_forecast_remaining_sensor: Sensor providing solar production still expected today in kWh. Saving it replaces the legacy whole-day forecast and it is never reduced by production already measured.
data_description.solar_production_sensor: Real-time PV production power sensor (W/kW) from an external inverter not wired through the battery MPPT inputs. Used to show the Solar node in the dashboard energy-flow diagram. Leave empty if your panels feed the battery MPPT directly.
data_description.meter_inverted: Enable this option if your meter uses the opposite convention: positive = export, negative = import. The unit (W/kW) is detected automatically.
data_description.max_contracted_power: Total contracted power in watts. System won't exceed this limit when charging to avoid tripping the breaker
data_description.three_phase_enabled: Optional safety envelope for three-phase installations. Configure one signed RMS current sensor in A, one fuse-size limit in A and the physical battery phase for each circuit in the next step.

three_phase.title: Three-phase current protection
three_phase.description: Configure one signed RMS current sensor and one fuse-size limit in amperes for each phase you want to protect. Leave both fields empty for unused phases. Sensors must be distinct Home Assistant sensor entities with A or mA units; positive means grid import and negative means grid export.

data_description.phase_1_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L1. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_2_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L2. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_3_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L3. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_1_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L1 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.
data_description.phase_2_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L2 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.
data_description.phase_3_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L3 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.

phase_assignments.title: Battery {battery_num} phase assignment
phase_assignments.description: Select the physical AC phase where {battery_name} is connected, or choose Unassigned if it is not connected to a protected phase. Omnibattery cannot discover this wiring automatically.

batteries.title: Number of batteries
batteries.description: How many batteries do you have installed?

battery_brand.title: Battery {battery_num} — Brand
battery_brand.description: Select the brand and type of battery {battery_num}.

data_description.brand: Marstek Venus: Modbus TCP. Zendure SolarFlow: local HTTP (HEMS must be disabled for Omnibattery control). Anker SOLIX Solarbank Max AC / 4 E5000 Pro: Modbus TCP (enable Modbus TCP under Third-Party Control in the Anker app; only one Modbus client at a time). Sessy: local HTTP.

battery_connection.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Marstek)
battery_connection.description: Enter connection details and battery model for battery {battery_num}.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: IP address of the battery on your local network. Leave empty if you use a serial port.
data_description.slave_id: Modbus slave/unit id (default 1). Change only when a Modbus proxy maps several batteries to one IP:port using distinct slave ids.
data_description.battery_version: Select your battery model version. Ev2 for older models, Ev3 for newer models with updated register map, A (Venus A) or D (Venus D) for hybrid inverter models
data_description.serial_port: USB-RS485 adapter path, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM3. Fill this instead of the IP address to use Modbus RTU over serial; leave empty for TCP.

battery_connection_zendure.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Zendure)
battery_connection_zendure.description: Enter connection details for the Zendure SolarFlow battery {battery_num}. Keep HEMS disabled in the Zendure app for Omnibattery control.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: IP address of the Zendure device on your local network

battery_connection_hoymiles.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Hoymiles)
battery_connection_hoymiles.description: Enable MQTT Service in S-Miles Home and point it to Home Assistant's configured MQTT broker before continuing.

data_description.device_id: Hoymiles MQTT device ID, for example MSA-280024341346.
data_description.hoymiles_model: Use automatic discovery unless the device publishes an incorrect or generic model.

battery_connection_esphome.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (LilyGo/ESPHome)
battery_connection_esphome.description: Select the ESPHome device (LilyGo RS485 bridge) that exposes Marstek battery {battery_num}. It must run the marstek-lilygo-rs485 firmware with the stock entity names.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.esphome_device: The LilyGo T-CAN485 device flashed with the Marstek ESPHome firmware

battery_limits.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Limits
battery_limits.description: Enter power and SOC limits for battery {battery_num}.

data.dc_pv_connected: Solar panels are connected directly to this battery
data.track_mac: Re-find this battery by its MAC address if its IP address changes

data_description.max_charge_power: Maximum power allowed to charge the battery
data_description.max_discharge_power: Maximum power allowed to discharge the battery
data_description.max_soc: Maximum state of charge - battery won't charge above this value
data_description.min_soc: Minimum state of charge - battery won't discharge below this value
data_description.charge_hysteresis_percent: Always on (minimum 2%). After reaching the top, the battery won't charge again until SOC drops to (Max SOC − hysteresis). Ex: Max SOC 100% with 2% = no charge until 98%.
data_description.backup_offgrid_threshold: Offgrid load above this value is treated as an active backup event, excluding the battery from PD control. Set higher if you have permanent loads (router, cameras) on the offgrid port.
data_description.full_charge_voltage_taper_enabled: When the target is 100%, limit charge to 200 W from 3.48 V max cell voltage. Venus E models stop at 3.60 V to measure imbalance after 60 seconds; Venus A/D with coupled packs keep charging at 200 W until the BMS cuts off.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Nominal usable capacity of the battery pack. Used to calculate stored energy and efficiency from SOC. Sessy requires its actual capacity; for other batteries, leave at 0 if unknown.
data_description.battery_phase: Physical AC phase (L1/L2/L3) where this battery is wired, or Unassigned when it is outside the protected phase layout. An unassigned battery is outside the three-phase envelope and continues normal automatic operation.
data_description.dc_pv_connected: Venus A/D only. Enable this when solar panels are wired to the battery's MPPT inputs. Disable it when those inputs are unused so battery power remains based on AC power without adding MPPT production.
data_description.track_mac: The MAC address is the battery's permanent hardware address: unlike the IP address above, it never changes. Home Assistant uses it to find the battery again and update the IP address by itself. Behind a Wi-Fi-to-LAN bridge or a powerline adapter the address you see is the adapter's own, shared with everything behind it, so tracking only works while a single battery sits behind that adapter.
data_description.mac: Permanent hardware address of the interface the battery uses on your network. Take it from your router's device list: a battery can report a different MAC than the one its wired interface actually uses. Filled in automatically when Home Assistant's DHCP cache is available.

time_slots.title: Time slots
time_slots.description: Do you want to configure time slots? Each slot can independently control when batteries are allowed to charge or discharge. Without slots, they operate at all times.

add_time_slot.title: Time slot {slot_num}
add_time_slot.description: Define when and how the batteries are allowed to operate. The ticks control each direction, SOC and power. Manual mode forces an exact power, bypassing the PD algorithm.

data_description.start_time: Slot start time (24h). Midnight crossing supported.
data_description.battery_scope: Select 'all' to apply to every battery, or pick a specific one.
data_description.allow_charge: If checked, charge is allowed during the slot. If NO slot allows charge, charge is unrestricted by default.
data_description.allow_discharge: If checked, discharge is allowed during the slot. If NO slot allows discharge, discharge is unrestricted by default.
data_description.soc_override_enabled: If checked, the slot overrides the battery's max/min SOC inside the window.
data_description.power_override_enabled: If checked, the slot limits or forces the max power.
data_description.mode: PD: the predictive algorithm caps power using the slot value. Manual: forced discharge or charge at the configured power.

add_time_slot_details.title: Slot {slot_num} details
add_time_slot_details.description: Configure SOC and/or power limits per battery. Every battery has its own sliders. Mapping: {battery_map}. SOC min range: 12–30%. SOC max range: 80–100%. Power range: 100 W up to each battery’s hardware max.

add_more_slots.title: Add more time slots
add_more_slots.description: You currently have {current_slots} configured slot(s). You can add up to {max_slots} slots in total.

excluded_devices.title: Special Device Management
excluded_devices.description: Configure devices with special management: you can EXCLUDE devices that should NOT be powered by battery, or ADD devices that SHOULD be powered by battery even if they're not in the home consumption sensor.

add_excluded_device.title: Special Device {device_num}
add_excluded_device.description: Configure how the battery should manage this device.

data.included_in_consumption: Consumption is included in home consumption sensor
data.allow_solar_surplus: Allow to use solar surplus (do not charge battery)
data.cover_home_when_active: Cover home while device is active

data_description.power_sensor: Numeric power sensor (W) for the device. Optional for EV chargers without power telemetry; existing configurations that stored the charging-state sensor here remain supported.
data_description.activity_sensor: State or binary sensor that becomes 'on' or reports 'Charging'/'Cargando' when the device requests power. Required for Dynamic Power Control and for a new EV charger without power telemetry.
data_description.included_in_consumption: ✓ CHECKED = Home sensor ALREADY includes this device → Battery will NOT power it (excluded). ✗ UNCHECKED = Home sensor doesn't see it → Battery WILL power it (additional)
data_description.allow_solar_surplus: If checked, the device will be able to consume energy directly from solar panels (surplus) without the battery trying to compensate. Recommended for high consumption devices like EV chargers.
data_description.dynamic_power_control: Enable for devices that automatically adjust their own demand from the grid meter, such as a solar-surplus wallbox. If an activity sensor is configured, Omnibattery yields before power appears; otherwise it reacts to the power sensor. It then uses genuine leftover export.
data_description.cover_home_when_active: Requires Solar Surplus and a solar-production sensor. The battery may cover the home's own load while this device is active; only the device's grid share stays excluded.
data_description.ev_charger_no_telemetry: ✓ CHECKED = Use the Activity / EV charging sensor instead of numeric power telemetry. Existing configurations that placed this state sensor in Device power sensor continue to work. When charging is detected, the battery pauses for 5 minutes; afterwards it may only charge from solar surplus and never discharges for the EV.

add_more_excluded_devices.title: Add more excluded devices
add_more_excluded_devices.description: You currently have {current_devices} excluded device(s). You can add up to {max_devices} devices total.

predictive_charging.title: Predictive Grid Charging
predictive_charging.description: Do you want to enable intelligent grid charging? This feature allows charging batteries from the grid during off-peak hours when today's solar forecast is insufficient.

predictive_charging_mode.title: Predictive Charging Mode
predictive_charging_mode.description: Select how the system decides when to charge from the grid.

data_description.predictive_charging_mode: Time Slot: charge during a fixed nightly window. Dynamic Pricing: automatically select the cheapest hours from a price sensor. Real-Time Price: activate charging instantly whenever the current price is below a threshold — no scheduling needed.

predictive_charging_config.title: Predictive Charging — Time Slot
predictive_charging_config.description: Configure when and how to charge batteries from the grid based on solar forecast. You can set up to 3 charging windows — fill only window 1 to keep a single window, or add windows 2 and 3 as needed.

data_description.start_time: Start time of charging window (e.g., 01:00, off-peak tariff)
data_description.days: Days when grid charging is allowed
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. If you have no solar panels, leave this empty — the system will charge whenever battery energy is not enough for the day. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

dynamic_pricing_config.title: Predictive Charging — Dynamic Pricing
dynamic_pricing_config.description: Configure the electricity price sensor and parameters for automatic cheap-hour selection.

data.dp_price_discharge_control: Only discharge when price is above threshold

data_description.price_integration_type: Select your electricity price provider integration. Nord Pool supports both the official Home Assistant integration and HACS. Tibber is service-based, so its price sensor can be left empty.
data_description.price_sensor: Sensor providing electricity prices (e.g., the official Nord Pool current-price sensor, a HACS Nordpool sensor, sensor.esios_pvpc for PVPC, or your CKW sensor for Switzerland)
data_description.max_price_threshold: Slots above this price will not be selected. When price-gated discharge is enabled, this value is also used as the discharge threshold unless a separate discharge floor is set below. Use major currency/kWh: €/kWh for Nordpool/PVPC, CHF/kWh for CKW. HACS Nordpool prices configured in cents are converted automatically. Leave empty to use all slots and use the daily average as the discharge threshold.
data_description.discharge_price_threshold: Optional separate floor for price-gated discharge. Discharge is blocked while the price is at or below this value, opening an idle band between the charge ceiling above and this floor: in that band the battery neither grid-charges nor discharges (solar-surplus charging still works). Leave empty to reuse the maximum price threshold for both (current single-threshold behavior).
data_description.dp_price_discharge_control: When enabled, the battery only discharges when the current electricity price exceeds the configured maximum price threshold. If no threshold is configured, it uses today's average price computed automatically from the price sensor. If time slots restrict discharge, both conditions must be met.
data_description.negative_price_charging_enabled: Opt-in dynamic-pricing feature that charges during the most negative import-price slots even when the normal energy forecast does not require grid charging. A solar forecast sensor is not required.
data_description.smart_predischarge_enabled: Opt-in dynamic-pricing anti-curtailment. It creates headroom before forecast PV reaches a negative-price window while preserving all SOC, user and battery safety limits.
data_description.negative_injection_threshold: Protect slots whose normalized price is at or below this inclusive threshold when forecast PV exceeds estimated household consumption.
data_description.predischarge_reserve_soc: Additional SOC floor for pre-discharge. 0 uses the configured and guaranteed minimum SOC floors.
data_description.predischarge_export_mode: Choose how deliberate grid export creates headroom: Self-consumption only (0 W), Automatic (only the power needed), or Custom limit (configured in the next step). The value is a deliberate-export limit, not total battery discharge power.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. If you have no solar panels, leave this empty — the system will charge whenever battery energy is not enough for the day. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

predischarge_export_limit.title: Anti-curtailment — Custom export limit
predischarge_export_limit.description: Set the maximum deliberate export to the grid while creating headroom. This is an export limit, not the battery's total discharge power.

data_description.predischarge_max_export_power_w: Maximum power that may be deliberately exported to the grid before a solar-risk window. Battery SOC, reserve, hardware power and existing locks remain authoritative.

realtime_price_config.title: Predictive Charging — Real-Time Price
realtime_price_config.description: Configure the price sensor and threshold. The system reads the current price every few seconds and starts or stops grid charging immediately — no daily schedule needed.

data.rt_price_discharge_control: Only discharge when price is above threshold

data_description.price_sensor: Sensor whose state is the current electricity price (e.g. sensor.esios_pvpc, sensor.nordpool_kwh_es_eur_3_10_0). Any sensor that exposes the current period price as its state works.
data_description.max_price_threshold: Charging activates when the current price is at or below this value. Use major currency/kWh (e.g. €/kWh for Nordpool/PVPC, CHF/kWh for CKW). HACS Nordpool prices configured in cents are converted automatically. Leave empty if using the daily average sensor below.
data_description.average_price_sensor: If provided, this sensor's state is used as the threshold instead of the fixed value above — useful when your price integration already exposes a daily average. Leave empty to use the fixed threshold.
data_description.rt_price_discharge_control: When enabled, the battery only discharges when the current electricity price exceeds the threshold (fixed or daily average). If time slots restrict discharge, both conditions must be met.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

weekly_full_charge.title: Weekly Full Charge
weekly_full_charge.description: Do you want to enable weekly full battery charge for cell balancing? This feature charges batteries to 100% once per week to balance the cells.

weekly_full_charge_config.title: Weekly Full Charge Configuration
weekly_full_charge_config.description: Select the day of the week when batteries should charge to 100% for cell balancing. After reaching 100%, the system reverts to your configured maximum charge limit.

data_description.weekly_full_charge_day: Day when batteries will charge to 100% regardless of configured max SOC. This helps balance battery cells.

charge_delay.title: Solar charge delay
charge_delay.description: Enable solar charge delay? This delays battery charging until the solar energy balance indicates it's needed, exporting excess solar to grid in the meantime.

charge_delay_config.title: Charge delay configuration
charge_delay_config.description: Configure the safety margin and solar forecast sensor for the charge delay.

data_description.delay_safety_margin_h: Hours before sunset by which charging must be complete. Higher values unlock charging earlier.
data_description.delay_soc_setpoint_enabled: When enabled, the battery charges freely up to the configured SOC; above it the solar delay activates.
data_description.delay_soc_setpoint: The SOC the battery must reach before the solar delay kicks in. Minimum is 12 % — the Venus battery minimum discharge SOC.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.

temp_charge_limit.title: Temperature charge limit
temp_charge_limit.description: Reduce charge power when a battery gets hot? Above a temperature limit charging is throttled proportionally and restored as the battery cools.

temp_charge_limit_config.title: Temperature charge limit configuration
temp_charge_limit_config.description: Set the temperature at which charging starts to throttle, the band over which it ramps down, and the minimum charge power (as a percentage of normal).

data_description.temp_charge_limit_c: Charging runs at full power at or below this temperature; above it the derate begins.
data_description.temp_charge_limit_band_c: Temperature range above the limit over which charge power ramps down to the minimum.
data_description.temp_charge_limit_floor_pct: Charge power at the limit plus the band, as a percentage of the normal charge ceiling. 0% stops charging entirely when very hot.
data_description.temp_limit_apply_discharge: Apply the same temperature derate to discharge power. Discharge tolerates heat better, so this shares the charge threshold as a compromise; mainly it keeps discharge under the BMS hard cutoff.

capacity_protection.title: Peak Shaving Mode
capacity_protection.description: When enabled, if battery SOC drops below a threshold, the system conserves energy by only discharging to offset consumption above a peak limit.

capacity_protection_config.title: Peak Shaving Configuration
capacity_protection_config.description: Configure the SOC threshold below which peak shaving activates, and the peak power limit. The battery will only discharge to keep grid import at or below the peak limit.

data_description.capacity_protection_soc_threshold: When average battery SOC drops below this value, peak shaving activates. The battery will stop discharging for normal consumption and only cover peaks above the limit.
data_description.capacity_protection_limit: Grid import power threshold. When house consumption exceeds this value and peak shaving is active, the battery discharges only the excess above this limit.

hourly_balance.title: Hourly Net Balance
hourly_balance.description:
Enable hourly net balance control? This feature tracks grid import/export per hour and automatically adjusts the battery setpoint to achieve a target net energy balance.

⚠️ **This feature is only useful in Spain**, under the hourly surplus-compensation scheme (Royal Decree 244/2019), where grid surplus is settled hour by hour. In markets with feed-in tariffs or annual net metering it provides no benefit and may cause lost export revenue and unnecessary battery cycling.

Detected Home Assistant country: **{country}**.

pd_advanced.title: Advanced PD Controller Parameters
pd_advanced.description: Configure advanced PD controller parameters for expert tuning of battery charge/discharge behavior. Only modify these if you understand PID control theory. Default values work well for most installations.

pd_advanced_config.title: PD Controller Configuration
pd_advanced_config.description: Tune the Proportional-Derivative controller that manages battery power adjustments.

data_description.pd_kp: Responsiveness to grid imbalance. Higher values = faster response but risk of overshoot. Range: 0.1-2.0, default: 0.65
data_description.pd_kd: Damping to prevent oscillation. Higher values = smoother transitions but slower settling. Range: 0.0-2.0, default: 0.5
data_description.pd_deadband: Grid power tolerance around zero. Prevents micro-adjustments to minor fluctuations. Range: 0-200W, default: 40W
data_description.pd_max_power_change: Maximum battery power change per control cycle (2.5s). Prevents abrupt commands. Range: 100-2000W, default: 800W
data_description.pd_direction_hysteresis: Power threshold required to switch between charging and discharging. Prevents rapid direction changes. Range: 0-200W, default: 60W
data_description.pd_min_charge_power: Minimum power for charging. Below this threshold, the controller stays idle instead of charging at low power. 0 = disabled.
data_description.pd_min_discharge_power: Minimum power for discharging. Below this threshold, the controller stays idle instead of discharging at low power. 0 = disabled.
data_description.pd_target_grid_power: Grid power setpoint the controller regulates to. Positive = import from grid (battery charges), negative = export to grid (battery discharges), 0 = net zero. The range follows your total configured battery power, narrowed by the system power limits when enabled. Default: 0 W.
data_description.enable_system_power_limits: When enabled, the two sliders below cap the combined charge/discharge power of all active batteries.
data_description.system_max_charge_power: Optional cap for combined charge power across all active batteries. 0 = disabled; per-battery limits still apply.
data_description.system_max_discharge_power: Optional cap for combined discharge power across all active batteries. 0 = disabled; per-battery limits still apply.

hourly_balance_config.title: Hourly Balance Configuration
hourly_balance_config.description: Configure the target net energy balance and control parameters. The system will adjust battery power to achieve the target Wh balance each hour.

data_description.hourly_balance_target_net_wh: Target net energy balance per hour. 0 = net zero (default). Positive = allow import, negative = target export.
data_description.hourly_balance_max_offset_w: Maximum power offset the controller can apply. The slider ceiling is the combined discharge power of all configured batteries.
data_description.hourly_balance_deadband_wh: Tolerance band around the target. No correction is applied when the net balance is within ±N kWh of the target. 0 = exact correction.
data_description.hourly_balance_hysteresis_w: Minimum change in offset required before a new correction is applied. Prevents micro-adjustments every cycle. 0 = apply every cycle. Default: 15 W.

reconfigure_battery.title: Reconfigure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Marstek)
reconfigure_battery.description: Update connection details for battery {battery_num}. Power limits, SOC limits and all other settings are preserved.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: New IP address of the battery on your local network. Leave empty if you use a serial port.
data_description.slave_id: Modbus slave/unit id (default 1). Change only when a Modbus proxy maps several batteries to one IP:port using distinct slave ids.
data_description.serial_port: USB-RS485 adapter path, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM3. Fill this instead of the IP address to use Modbus RTU over serial; leave empty for TCP.

reconfigure_battery_zendure.title: Reconfigure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Zendure)

battery_connection_huawei.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Huawei)
battery_connection_huawei.description:
Omnibattery reads this battery over Modbus and sends its set-points through the Huawei Solar integration, so it needs both: a Modbus endpoint and the battery device. Point the Modbus address at a Modbus proxy rather than straight at the inverter — the Huawei Solar integration already holds a connection to it.

A Huawei inverter accepts only ONE Modbus connection at a time. If anything else talks to it besides Omnibattery — the Huawei Solar integration, evcc, another system — you need a Modbus proxy in front that fans the connection out to several clients, for example {proxy_url}. Enter the proxy's address and port instead of the inverter's. The slave id is searched for automatically when the one entered does not answer.

error.invalid_mac: That does not look like a MAC address. Six pairs of hexadecimal digits are expected, for example dc:04:5a:14:6b:33.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the battery. Check the IP address and that the battery is accessible on the network.
error.no_battery: Inverter reached, but it reports no battery. Check that the LUNA2000 is attached and the Modbus slave ID points at the inverter.
error.huawei_device_required: Without direct Modbus writes, Omnibattery controls the battery through the Huawei Solar integration's services, and those address it by device. Either pick the device or enable direct writes.
error.huawei_solar_missing: Without direct Modbus writes, Omnibattery controls the battery through the Huawei Solar integration's services — but that integration is not set up here. Install and configure it via HACS, or enable direct writes.
error.huawei_device_mismatch: The chosen battery device belongs to a different inverter than the Modbus address points at. With cascaded inverters the readings would come from one unit while the commands landed on another. Check the device and the slave id.
error.esphome_entities_missing: The selected ESPHome device is missing required entities: {missing}. Make sure it runs the marstek-lilygo-rs485 firmware with the stock entity names.
error.sensor_not_found: Solar forecast sensor does not exist. Verify the sensor is available.
error.invalid_unit: Solar forecast sensor must have 'kWh' or 'Wh' as unit.
error.solar_production_sensor_not_found: Solar production sensor does not exist. Verify the sensor is available.
error.solar_production_invalid_unit: Solar production sensor must have 'W' or 'kW' as unit.
error.solar_production_sensor_circular: A solar sensor created by OmniBattery cannot be reused as an external solar production input.
error.offgrid_sensor_must_differ: The off-grid power sensor must differ from the normal grid sensor.
error.offgrid_sensor_not_found: The off-grid power sensor does not exist or is unavailable.
error.offgrid_sensor_invalid_unit: The off-grid power sensor must have 'W' or 'kW' as unit.
error.phase_sensors_must_differ: Each phase must use a different current sensor.
error.phase_sensor_not_found: The phase current sensor does not exist or is unavailable.
error.phase_sensor_invalid_domain: The phase current source must be a sensor entity.
error.phase_sensor_invalid_unit: The phase current sensor must have 'A' or 'mA' as unit.
error.phase_limit_must_be_positive: The phase fuse size must be a positive finite value in amperes.
error.phase_sensor_and_limit_required: Set both the phase current sensor and its fuse size, or leave both fields empty.
error.battery_phase_required: Select the physical phase for this battery.
error.incomplete_window: Each extra charging window needs both a start and an end time. Fill both, or leave both empty to skip it.
error.overlapping_slots: This time slot overlaps with an existing one for the same battery. Adjust the times, days, or battery scope.
error.midnight_crossing: Start time must be before end time. For overnight periods, create two separate slots (e.g., 22:00-23:59 and 00:00-06:00).
error.slot_does_nothing: The slot must allow at least one direction (charge or discharge).
error.manual_requires_power: Manual mode requires the power override tick to be enabled.
error.no_price_data: Selected sensor is not a supported price source. Nord Pool: select an entity from the official integration or a HACS sensor with `raw_today`. PVPC: needs `price_00h` … `price_23h`. CKW: needs a `prices` list. EPEX: needs a `data` list. ENTSO-e: needs a `prices_today` list.
error.tibber_unavailable: The Tibber integration is not installed, or its `tibber.get_prices` service is unavailable. Install and configure Tibber first.
error.discharge_below_charge: The discharge price floor cannot be below the maximum (charge) price threshold. Set it equal or higher, or leave it empty to reuse the charge threshold.
error.host_or_serial_required: Enter either an IP address (TCP) or a serial port path (Modbus RTU).
error.missing_power_sensor: Select a device power sensor, or enable EV charger without power telemetry and select an activity sensor.
error.missing_activity_sensor: Select an Activity / EV charging sensor for Dynamic Power Control or an EV charger without power telemetry.

init.title: Reconfigure Omnibattery
init.description: Select which section you want to configure.

sensors.title: Sensors
sensors.description: Configure the sensors used by the integration.

data_description.consumption_sensor: Real-time sensor for imported (+) or exported (-) grid power. Updates every 1-2 seconds are recommended. Slower sensors are accepted, but delayed readings reduce regulation quality; the latest reading is followed for up to 65 seconds.
data_description.offgrid_power_sensor: Separate W/kW meter for the backed-up circuit. It must differ from the normal grid sensor. Configuring it exposes a software switch that selects this source for control and statistics; it does not enable the battery's physical off-grid/EPS port.
data_description.offgrid_meter_inverted: Enable when the off-grid sensor uses the opposite convention: positive = export and negative = consumption. This setting applies only while off-grid meter mode is active.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Legacy sensor providing the whole-day solar forecast. Existing installations can keep using it during the transition; prefer Remaining Today for new configurations.
data_description.solar_forecast_remaining_sensor: Sensor providing solar production still expected today in kWh. Saving it replaces the legacy whole-day forecast and it is never reduced by production already measured.
data_description.solar_production_sensor: Real-time PV production power sensor (W/kW) from an external inverter not wired through the battery MPPT inputs. Used to show the Solar node in the dashboard energy-flow diagram. Leave empty if your panels feed the battery MPPT directly.
data_description.meter_inverted: Enable this option if your meter uses the opposite convention: positive = export, negative = import. The unit (W/kW) is detected automatically.
data_description.max_contracted_power: Total contracted power in watts. System won't exceed this limit when charging to avoid tripping the breaker
data_description.three_phase_enabled: Optional safety envelope for three-phase installations. Configure one signed RMS current sensor in A, one fuse-size limit in A and the physical battery phase for each circuit in the next step.

three_phase.title: Three-phase current protection
three_phase.description: Configure one signed RMS current sensor and one fuse-size limit in amperes for each phase you want to protect. Leave both fields empty for unused phases. Sensors must be distinct Home Assistant sensor entities with A or mA units; positive means grid import and negative means grid export.

data_description.phase_1_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L1. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_2_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L2. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_3_current_sensor: Real-time signed RMS current on physical phase L3. Positive import, negative export; A and mA are accepted.
data_description.phase_1_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L1 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.
data_description.phase_2_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L2 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.
data_description.phase_3_fuse_size: Fuse rating/current limit for L3 in amperes. Enter a value below the nameplate rating to leave margin for latency and transient peaks.

phase_assignments.title: Battery {battery_num} phase assignment
phase_assignments.description: Select the physical AC phase where {battery_name} is connected, or choose Unassigned if it is not connected to a protected phase. Omnibattery cannot discover this wiring automatically.

batteries.description: Modify the number of batteries. If you reduce the number, the last configured batteries will be removed.

battery_limits.description: Modify power and SOC limits for battery {battery_num}.

data.dc_pv_connected: Solar panels are connected directly to this battery
data.track_mac: Re-find this battery by its MAC address if its IP address changes

data_description.max_charge_power: Maximum power allowed to charge the battery
data_description.max_discharge_power: Maximum power allowed to discharge the battery
data_description.charge_hysteresis_percent: Always on (minimum 2%). After reaching the top, the battery won't charge again until SOC drops to (Max SOC − hysteresis). Ex: Max SOC 100% with 2% = no charge until 98%.
data_description.backup_offgrid_threshold: Offgrid load above this value is treated as an active backup event, excluding the battery from PD control. Set higher if you have permanent loads (router, cameras) on the offgrid port.
data_description.full_charge_voltage_taper_enabled: When the target is 100%, limit charge to 200 W from 3.48 V max cell voltage. Venus E models stop at 3.60 V to measure imbalance after 60 seconds; Venus A/D with coupled packs keep charging at 200 W until the BMS cuts off.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Nominal usable capacity of the battery pack. Used to calculate stored energy and efficiency from SOC. Sessy requires its actual capacity; for other batteries, leave at 0 if unknown.
data_description.battery_phase: Physical AC phase (L1/L2/L3) where this battery is wired, or Unassigned when it is outside the protected phase layout. An unassigned battery is outside the three-phase envelope and continues normal automatic operation.
data_description.dc_pv_connected: Venus A/D only. Enable this when solar panels are wired to the battery's MPPT inputs. Disable it when those inputs are unused so battery power remains based on AC power without adding MPPT production.
data_description.track_mac: The MAC address is the battery's permanent hardware address: unlike the IP address above, it never changes. Home Assistant uses it to find the battery again and update the IP address by itself. Behind a Wi-Fi-to-LAN bridge or a powerline adapter the address you see is the adapter's own, shared with everything behind it, so tracking only works while a single battery sits behind that adapter.
data_description.mac: Permanent hardware address of the interface the battery uses on your network. Take it from your router's device list: a battery can report a different MAC than the one its wired interface actually uses. Filled in automatically when Home Assistant's DHCP cache is available.

time_slots.title: Time slots
time_slots.description: Do you want to reconfigure time slots? Each slot can independently control charge and discharge. If unchecked, all slots will be removed (batteries will operate at all times).

add_time_slot.title: Time slot {slot_num}
add_time_slot.description: Define when and how the batteries are allowed to operate. The ticks control each direction, SOC and power. Manual mode forces an exact power, bypassing the PD algorithm.

data_description.start_time: Slot start time (24h). Midnight crossing supported.
data_description.battery_scope: Select 'all' to apply to every battery, or pick a specific one.
data_description.allow_charge: If checked, charge is allowed during the slot. If NO slot allows charge, charge is unrestricted by default.
data_description.allow_discharge: If checked, discharge is allowed during the slot. If NO slot allows discharge, discharge is unrestricted by default.
data_description.soc_override_enabled: If checked, the slot overrides the battery's max/min SOC inside the window.
data_description.power_override_enabled: If checked, the slot limits or forces the max power.
data_description.mode: PD: the predictive algorithm caps power using the slot value. Manual: forced discharge or charge at the configured power.

add_time_slot_details.title: Slot {slot_num} details
add_time_slot_details.description: Configure SOC and/or power limits per battery. Every battery has its own sliders. Mapping: {battery_map}. SOC min range: 12–30%. SOC max range: 80–100%. Power range: 100 W up to each battery’s hardware max.

add_more_slots.title: Add more time slots
add_more_slots.description: You have {current_slots} configured slot(s). You can add up to {max_slots} in total.

excluded_devices.title: Special Device Management
excluded_devices.description: Configure devices with special management: you can EXCLUDE devices that should NOT be powered by battery, or ADD devices that SHOULD be powered by battery even if they're not in the home consumption sensor.

add_excluded_device.title: Special Device {device_num}
add_excluded_device.description: Configure how the battery should manage this device.

data.included_in_consumption: Consumption is included in home consumption sensor
data.allow_solar_surplus: Allow to use solar surplus (do not charge battery)
data.cover_home_when_active: Cover home while device is active

data_description.power_sensor: Numeric power sensor (W) for the device. Optional for EV chargers without power telemetry; existing configurations that stored the charging-state sensor here remain supported.
data_description.activity_sensor: State or binary sensor that becomes 'on' or reports 'Charging'/'Cargando' when the device requests power. Required for Dynamic Power Control and for a new EV charger without power telemetry.
data_description.included_in_consumption: ✓ CHECKED = Home sensor ALREADY includes this device → Battery will NOT power it (excluded). ✗ UNCHECKED = Home sensor doesn't see it → Battery WILL power it (additional)
data_description.allow_solar_surplus: If checked, the device will be able to consume energy directly from solar panels (surplus) without the battery trying to compensate. Recommended for high consumption devices like EV chargers.
data_description.dynamic_power_control: Enable for devices that automatically adjust their own demand from the grid meter, such as a solar-surplus wallbox. If an activity sensor is configured, Omnibattery yields before power appears; otherwise it reacts to the power sensor. It then uses genuine leftover export.
data_description.cover_home_when_active: Requires Solar Surplus and a solar-production sensor. The battery may cover the home's own load while this device is active; only the device's grid share stays excluded.
data_description.ev_charger_no_telemetry: ✓ CHECKED = Use the Activity / EV charging sensor instead of numeric power telemetry. Existing configurations that placed this state sensor in Device power sensor continue to work. When charging is detected, the battery pauses for 5 minutes; afterwards it may only charge from solar surplus and never discharges for the EV.

add_more_excluded_devices.title: Add more excluded devices
add_more_excluded_devices.description: You have {current_devices} excluded device(s). You can add up to {max_devices} in total.

predictive_charging.title: Predictive Grid Charging
predictive_charging.description: Do you want to enable intelligent grid charging? This feature allows charging batteries from the grid during off-peak hours when today's solar forecast is insufficient.

predictive_charging_mode.title: Predictive Charging Mode
predictive_charging_mode.description: Select how the system decides when to charge from the grid.

data_description.predictive_charging_mode: Time Slot: charge during a fixed nightly window. Dynamic Pricing: automatically select the cheapest hours from a price sensor. Real-Time Price: activate charging instantly whenever the current price is below a threshold — no scheduling needed.

predictive_charging_config.title: Predictive Charging — Time Slot
predictive_charging_config.description: Configure when and how to charge batteries from the grid based on solar forecast. You can set up to 3 charging windows — fill only window 1 to keep a single window, or add windows 2 and 3 as needed.

data_description.start_time: Start time of charging window (e.g., 01:00, off-peak tariff)
data_description.days: Days when grid charging is allowed
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. If you have no solar panels, leave this empty — the system will charge whenever battery energy is not enough for the day. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

dynamic_pricing_config.title: Predictive Charging — Dynamic Pricing
dynamic_pricing_config.description: Configure the electricity price sensor and parameters for automatic cheap-hour selection.

data.dp_price_discharge_control: Only discharge when price is above threshold

data_description.price_integration_type: Select your electricity price provider integration. Nord Pool supports both the official Home Assistant integration and HACS. Tibber is service-based, so its price sensor can be left empty.
data_description.price_sensor: Sensor providing electricity prices (e.g., the official Nord Pool current-price sensor, a HACS Nordpool sensor, sensor.esios_pvpc for PVPC, or your CKW sensor for Switzerland)
data_description.max_price_threshold: Slots above this price will not be selected. When price-gated discharge is enabled, this value is also used as the discharge threshold unless a separate discharge floor is set below. Use major currency/kWh: €/kWh for Nordpool/PVPC, CHF/kWh for CKW. HACS Nordpool prices configured in cents are converted automatically. Leave empty to use all slots and use the daily average as the discharge threshold.
data_description.discharge_price_threshold: Optional separate floor for price-gated discharge. Discharge is blocked while the price is at or below this value, opening an idle band between the charge ceiling above and this floor: in that band the battery neither grid-charges nor discharges (solar-surplus charging still works). Leave empty to reuse the maximum price threshold for both (current single-threshold behavior).
data_description.dp_price_discharge_control: When enabled, the battery only discharges when the current electricity price exceeds the configured maximum price threshold. If no threshold is configured, it uses today's average price computed automatically from the price sensor. If time slots restrict discharge, both conditions must be met.
data_description.negative_price_charging_enabled: Opt-in dynamic-pricing feature that charges during the most negative import-price slots even when the normal energy forecast does not require grid charging. A solar forecast sensor is not required.
data_description.smart_predischarge_enabled: Opt-in dynamic-pricing anti-curtailment. It creates headroom before forecast PV reaches a negative-price window while preserving all SOC, user and battery safety limits.
data_description.negative_injection_threshold: Protect slots whose normalized price is at or below this inclusive threshold when forecast PV exceeds estimated household consumption.
data_description.predischarge_reserve_soc: Additional SOC floor for pre-discharge. 0 uses the configured and guaranteed minimum SOC floors.
data_description.predischarge_export_mode: Choose how deliberate grid export creates headroom: Self-consumption only (0 W), Automatic (only the power needed), or Custom limit (configured in the next step). The value is a deliberate-export limit, not total battery discharge power.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. If you have no solar panels, leave this empty — the system will charge whenever battery energy is not enough for the day. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

predischarge_export_limit.title: Anti-curtailment — Custom export limit
predischarge_export_limit.description: Set the maximum deliberate export to the grid while creating headroom. This is an export limit, not the battery's total discharge power.

data_description.predischarge_max_export_power_w: Maximum power that may be deliberately exported to the grid before a solar-risk window. Battery SOC, reserve, hardware power and existing locks remain authoritative.

realtime_price_config.title: Predictive Charging — Real-Time Price
realtime_price_config.description: Configure the price sensor and threshold. The system reads the current price every few seconds and starts or stops grid charging immediately — no daily schedule needed.

data.rt_price_discharge_control: Only discharge when price is above threshold

data_description.price_sensor: Sensor whose state is the current electricity price (e.g. sensor.esios_pvpc, sensor.nordpool_kwh_es_eur_3_10_0). Any sensor that exposes the current period price as its state works.
data_description.max_price_threshold: Charging activates when the current price is at or below this value. Use major currency/kWh (e.g. €/kWh for Nordpool/PVPC, CHF/kWh for CKW). HACS Nordpool prices configured in cents are converted automatically. Leave empty if using the daily average sensor below.
data_description.average_price_sensor: If provided, this sensor's state is used as the threshold instead of the fixed value above — useful when your price integration already exposes a daily average. Leave empty to use the fixed threshold.
data_description.rt_price_discharge_control: When enabled, the battery only discharges when the current electricity price exceeds the threshold (fixed or daily average). If time slots restrict discharge, both conditions must be met.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing the solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). If you have solar panels, configure this sensor — the system will only charge from the grid when solar forecast is insufficient. Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.
data_description.predictive_safety_margin_kwh: Extra energy buffer added to the consumption forecast before deciding whether to charge. The same kWh buffer is also reserved as additional anti-curtailment headroom in Dynamic Pricing. Set to 0 to disable (default). Capped at total battery capacity.
data_description.predictive_grid_charge_margin_pct: Extra % charged from the grid on top of the solar-deficit, to hedge against optimistic solar forecasts. E.g. a 2 kWh grid need at 50% charges 3 kWh. 0 to disable (default). Capped at the gap to max SOC.

weekly_full_charge.title: Weekly Full Charge
weekly_full_charge.description: Do you want to enable weekly full battery charge for cell balancing? This feature charges batteries to 100% once per week to balance the cells.

weekly_full_charge_config.title: Weekly Full Charge Configuration
weekly_full_charge_config.description: Select the day of the week when batteries should charge to 100% for cell balancing. After reaching 100%, the system reverts to your configured maximum charge limit.

data_description.weekly_full_charge_day: Day when batteries will charge to 100% regardless of configured max SOC. This helps balance battery cells.

charge_delay.title: Solar charge delay
charge_delay.description: Enable solar charge delay? This delays battery charging until the solar energy balance indicates it's needed, exporting excess solar to grid in the meantime.

charge_delay_config.title: Charge delay configuration
charge_delay_config.description: Configure the safety margin and solar forecast sensor for the charge delay.

data_description.delay_safety_margin_h: Hours before sunset by which charging must be complete. Higher values unlock charging earlier.
data_description.delay_soc_setpoint_enabled: When enabled, the battery charges freely up to the configured SOC; above it the solar delay activates.
data_description.delay_soc_setpoint: The SOC the battery must reach before the solar delay kicks in. Minimum is 12 % — the Venus battery minimum discharge SOC.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensor: Sensor providing solar production forecast in kWh (e.g., Solcast). Not required if you already configured this sensor in the initial setup step — it will be used automatically.

temp_charge_limit.title: Temperature charge limit
temp_charge_limit.description: Reduce charge power when a battery gets hot? Above a temperature limit charging is throttled proportionally and restored as the battery cools.

temp_charge_limit_config.title: Temperature charge limit configuration
temp_charge_limit_config.description: Set the temperature at which charging starts to throttle, the band over which it ramps down, and the minimum charge power (as a percentage of normal).

data_description.temp_charge_limit_c: Charging runs at full power at or below this temperature; above it the derate begins.
data_description.temp_charge_limit_band_c: Temperature range above the limit over which charge power ramps down to the minimum.
data_description.temp_charge_limit_floor_pct: Charge power at the limit plus the band, as a percentage of the normal charge ceiling. 0% stops charging entirely when very hot.
data_description.temp_limit_apply_discharge: Apply the same temperature derate to discharge power. Discharge tolerates heat better, so this shares the charge threshold as a compromise; mainly it keeps discharge under the BMS hard cutoff.

capacity_protection.title: Capacity Protection Mode
capacity_protection.description: When enabled, if battery SOC drops below a threshold, the system conserves energy by only discharging to offset consumption above a peak limit.

capacity_protection_config.title: Capacity Protection Configuration
capacity_protection_config.description: Configure the SOC threshold below which protection activates, and the peak power limit. The battery will only discharge to keep grid import at or below the peak limit.

data_description.capacity_protection_soc_threshold: When average battery SOC drops below this value, capacity protection activates. The battery will stop discharging for normal consumption and only cover peaks above the limit.
data_description.capacity_protection_limit: Grid import power threshold. When house consumption exceeds this value and protection is active, the battery discharges only the excess above this limit.

pd_advanced.title: Advanced PD Controller Parameters
pd_advanced.description: Configure advanced PD controller parameters for expert tuning of battery charge/discharge behavior. Only modify these if you understand PID control theory. Default values work well for most installations.

pd_advanced_config.title: PD Controller Configuration
pd_advanced_config.description: Tune the Proportional-Derivative controller that manages battery power adjustments. Changes will apply after integration reload.

data_description.pd_kp: Responsiveness to grid imbalance. Higher values = faster response but risk of overshoot. Range: 0.1-2.0, default: 0.65
data_description.pd_kd: Damping to prevent oscillation. Higher values = smoother transitions but slower settling. Range: 0.0-2.0, default: 0.5
data_description.pd_deadband: Grid power tolerance around zero. Prevents micro-adjustments to minor fluctuations. Higher values reduce sensitivity. Range: 0-200W, default: 40W
data_description.pd_max_power_change: Maximum battery power change per control cycle (2.5s). Prevents abrupt commands. Lower values = smoother but slower. Range: 100-2000W, default: 800W
data_description.pd_direction_hysteresis: Power threshold required to switch between charging and discharging. Prevents rapid direction changes. Range: 0-200W, default: 60W
data_description.pd_min_charge_power: Minimum power for charging. Below this threshold, the controller stays idle instead of charging at low power. 0 = disabled.
data_description.pd_min_discharge_power: Minimum power for discharging. Below this threshold, the controller stays idle instead of discharging at low power. 0 = disabled.
data_description.pd_target_grid_power: Grid power setpoint the controller regulates to. Positive = import from grid (battery charges), negative = export to grid (battery discharges), 0 = net zero. The range follows your total configured battery power, narrowed by the system power limits when enabled. Default: 0 W.
data_description.enable_system_power_limits: When enabled, the two sliders below cap the combined charge/discharge power of all active batteries.
data_description.system_max_charge_power: Optional cap for combined charge power across all active batteries. 0 = disabled; per-battery limits still apply.
data_description.system_max_discharge_power: Optional cap for combined discharge power across all active batteries. 0 = disabled; per-battery limits still apply.

hourly_balance.title: Hourly Net Balance
hourly_balance.description:
Enable hourly net balance control? This feature tracks grid import/export per hour and automatically adjusts the battery setpoint to achieve a target net energy balance.

⚠️ **This feature is only useful in Spain**, under the hourly surplus-compensation scheme (Royal Decree 244/2019), where grid surplus is settled hour by hour. In markets with feed-in tariffs or annual net metering it provides no benefit and may cause lost export revenue and unnecessary battery cycling.

Detected Home Assistant country: **{country}**.

hourly_balance_config.title: Hourly Balance Configuration
hourly_balance_config.description: Configure the target net energy balance and control parameters. The system will adjust battery power to achieve the target Wh balance each hour.

data_description.hourly_balance_target_net_wh: Target net energy balance per hour. 0 = net zero (default). Positive = allow import, negative = target export.
data_description.hourly_balance_max_offset_w: Maximum power offset the controller can apply. The slider ceiling is the combined discharge power of all configured batteries.
data_description.hourly_balance_deadband_wh: Tolerance band around the target. No correction is applied when the net balance is within ±N kWh of the target. 0 = exact correction.
data_description.hourly_balance_hysteresis_w: Minimum change in offset required before a new correction is applied. Prevents micro-adjustments every cycle. 0 = apply every cycle. Default: 15 W.

battery_connection_sessy.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Sessy)
battery_connection_sessy.description: Modify the connection details and local dongle credentials for the Sessy battery {battery_num}.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: IP address of the Sessy device on your local network
data_description.username: Local username printed on the Sessy dongle
data_description.password: Local password printed on the Sessy dongle

battery_connection_huawei.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Huawei)
battery_connection_huawei.description:
Modify the Modbus endpoint and the Huawei Solar battery device used for battery {battery_num}.

A Huawei inverter accepts only ONE Modbus connection at a time. If anything else talks to it besides Omnibattery — the Huawei Solar integration, evcc, another system — you need a Modbus proxy in front that fans the connection out to several clients, for example {proxy_url}. Enter the proxy's address and port instead of the inverter's. The slave id is searched for automatically when the one entered does not answer.

data.name: Name
data.slave_id: Modbus slave id (leave empty to search)

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: Address of the Modbus proxy or inverter Omnibattery reads from
data_description.slave_id: Unit id of the inverter — not of the energy manager or a charger. Leave it empty and setup goes looking: it tries the usual ids, identifies each inverter by its model register and takes the one with a battery attached. If several answer — Huawei inverters can be cascaded — a selection step follows. The search takes about 15 seconds.
data_description.huawei_battery_device: Only needed when direct Modbus writes are off, in which case set-points go through the Huawei Solar integration's services. With direct writes, leave it empty.
data_description.huawei_direct_write: Write set-points as Modbus registers instead of calling the Huawei Solar integration's services. Same register sequence, but without the detour through the service layer or the wait on that integration's communication lock. Off by default — enable it once the proven path is working.

battery_connection_huawei_slave.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Choose inverter
battery_connection_huawei_slave.description: {count} inverters with a battery answered on this Modbus endpoint. Huawei inverters can be cascaded — pick the one this battery belongs to. For a second battery, add another entry with the other slave id.

battery_connection_anker.title: Configure battery {battery_num} — Connection (Anker)
battery_connection_anker.description: Modify connection details for Anker SOLIX Solarbank Max AC / 4 E5000 Pro battery {battery_num}. Enable Modbus TCP under Third-Party Control in the Anker app first. Only one Modbus client can connect at a time.

data_description.name: Descriptive name to identify this battery
data_description.host: IP address shown in the Anker app under Third-Party Control

error.invalid_mac: That does not look like a MAC address. Six pairs of hexadecimal digits are expected, for example dc:04:5a:14:6b:33.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the battery. Check the IP address and that the battery is accessible on the network.
error.no_battery: Inverter reached, but it reports no battery. Check that the LUNA2000 is attached and the Modbus slave ID points at the inverter.
error.huawei_device_required: Without direct Modbus writes, Omnibattery controls the battery through the Huawei Solar integration's services, and those address it by device. Either pick the device or enable direct writes.
error.huawei_solar_missing: Without direct Modbus writes, Omnibattery controls the battery through the Huawei Solar integration's services — but that integration is not set up here. Install and configure it via HACS, or enable direct writes.
error.huawei_device_mismatch: The chosen battery device belongs to a different inverter than the Modbus address points at. With cascaded inverters the readings would come from one unit while the commands landed on another. Check the device and the slave id.
error.esphome_entities_missing: The selected ESPHome device is missing required entities: {missing}. Make sure it runs the marstek-lilygo-rs485 firmware with the stock entity names.
error.sensor_not_found: Solar forecast sensor does not exist. Verify the sensor is available.
error.invalid_unit: Solar forecast sensor must have 'kWh' or 'Wh' as unit.
error.solar_production_sensor_not_found: Solar production sensor does not exist. Verify the sensor is available.
error.solar_production_invalid_unit: Solar production sensor must have 'W' or 'kW' as unit.
error.solar_production_sensor_circular: A solar sensor created by OmniBattery cannot be reused as an external solar production input.
error.offgrid_sensor_must_differ: The off-grid power sensor must differ from the normal grid sensor.
error.offgrid_sensor_not_found: The off-grid power sensor does not exist or is unavailable.
error.offgrid_sensor_invalid_unit: The off-grid power sensor must have 'W' or 'kW' as unit.
error.phase_sensors_must_differ: Each phase must use a different current sensor.
error.phase_sensor_not_found: The phase current sensor does not exist or is unavailable.
error.phase_sensor_invalid_domain: The phase current source must be a sensor entity.
error.phase_sensor_invalid_unit: The phase current sensor must have 'A' or 'mA' as unit.
error.phase_limit_must_be_positive: The phase fuse size must be a positive finite value in amperes.
error.phase_sensor_and_limit_required: Set both the phase current sensor and its fuse size, or leave both fields empty.
error.battery_phase_required: Select the physical phase for this battery.
error.incomplete_window: Each extra charging window needs both a start and an end time. Fill both, or leave both empty to skip it.
error.overlapping_slots: This time slot overlaps with an existing one for the same battery. Adjust the times, days, or battery scope.
error.midnight_crossing: Start time must be before end time. For overnight periods, create two separate slots (e.g., 22:00-23:59 and 00:00-06:00).
error.slot_does_nothing: The slot must allow at least one direction (charge or discharge).
error.manual_requires_power: Manual mode requires the power override tick to be enabled.
error.no_price_data: Selected sensor is not a supported price source. Nord Pool: select an entity from the official integration or a HACS sensor with `raw_today`. PVPC: needs `price_00h` … `price_23h`. CKW: needs a `prices` list. EPEX: needs a `data` list. ENTSO-e: needs a `prices_today` list.
error.tibber_unavailable: The Tibber integration is not installed, or its `tibber.get_prices` service is unavailable. Install and configure Tibber first.
error.discharge_below_charge: The discharge price floor cannot be below the maximum (charge) price threshold. Set it equal or higher, or leave it empty to reuse the charge threshold.
error.host_or_serial_required: Enter either an IP address (TCP) or a serial port path (Modbus RTU).
error.missing_power_sensor: Select a device power sensor, or enable EV charger without power telemetry and select an activity sensor.
error.missing_activity_sensor: Select an Activity / EV charging sensor for Dynamic Power Control or an EV charger without power telemetry.

manual_control_required.message: {battery} is under automatic control, so Force Mode and the charge/discharge setpoints are rewritten every control cycle. Enable Manual Mode (system-wide or for this battery) before commanding it directly.
